The TBC system being studied is designated PWA264 and is currently in commercial aircraft revenue service.
The bond coat layer is a plasma-sprayed NiCoCrAlY metallic alloy, and the ceramic top layer is 7 wt% Y2O3-ZrO2 applied by air plasma spraying.

The primary mode of TBC failure is identified as ceramic spallation resulting from the formation of a dominant crack in the ceramic layer, parallel to but not coincident with the metal-ceramic interface.
Cyclic burner rig tests will be conducted at two cycle rates, on as-fabricated coatings and on coatings pre-exposed in oxidizing and non-oxidizing environments.
The influence of cyclic thermal stress level will be studied by varying peak test temperature, transient heating rate, and ceramic thickness.
The instrumented specimen design provides temperature measurements at the ceramic surface and 10 mils below the metal-ceramic interface in five circumferential locations.
Material property tests will be conducted on bulk ceramic and metallic (bond coat composition) specimens fabricated by plasma spraying thick coatings on mild steel panels.
The single rotating specimen test method used in Phase I verification and Phase II model development will improve temperature measurement and control, and eliminate circumferential thermal gradients.
Transient thermal and stress analyses using the MARC finite element program will be used to develop the life prediction models.
Dimensional analysis and multiple linear and nonlinear regression techniques will be used to correlate the test data and develop the life prediction models.
Analytical studies will be conducted to account for the effects of bond coat oxidation on the stress increase in the ceramic layer.
The Phase II models will include continuum and fracture mechanics approaches, as well as the effects of thermal exposure on component properties.
The validity of the Phase II models will be assessed through a series of benchmark engine mission simulation tests.
The research aims to develop an integrated, mechanistically-based life prediction model accounting for all relevant TBC degradation and failure modes.
The experimental program includes static furnace tests, cyclic burner rig tests, fractional exposure tests, and single rotating specimen tests.
